req.title: Return POST request metadata
req.statement: The system shall respond to POST /post with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that POST /post returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing exactly the keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, and origin. Tests are designed to: (1) verify the positive path with a form-encoded body, (2) verify the positive path with a JSON body, (3) verify the negative path using a disallowed HTTP method (GET on /post), (4) verify boundary behavior with an empty POST body, and (5) verify that query-string args are reflected correctly. Each test asserts exact values to maximize mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_post_form_data_returns_200_with_all_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: POST to /post with application/x-www-form-urlencoded body containing key=value
expected: JSON body contains exactly the keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, origin
form field reflects submitted key-value pair
data field is empty string for form submission
trace: R-HTTPBIN-004: JSON body reflecting POST payload; HTTP 200
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_form_data_returns_200_with_all_keys():
    r = client.post('/post', data={'mykey': 'myvalue'},
                    content_type='application/x-www-form-urlencoded')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'application/json' in r.content_type
    body = r.get_json()
    expected_keys = {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'form', 'data', 'files', 'json', 'origin'}
    assert set(body.keys()) == expected_keys
    assert body['form'] == {'mykey': 'myvalue'}
    assert body['data'] == ''
    assert body['json'] is None
    assert body['args'] == {}
    assert body['files'] == {}
    assert isinstance(body['headers'], dict)
    assert isinstance(body['url'], str)
    assert 'post' in body['url']

test_post_form_data_returns_200_with_all_keys()

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_with_query_args_reflected_in_args_field():
    r = client.post('/post?foo=bar&baz=qux')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['args'] == {'foo': 'bar', 'baz': 'qux'}
    assert body['form'] == {}
    assert body['json'] is None
    assert 'foo=bar' in body['url']
    assert 'baz=qux' in body['url']
    assert body['files'] == {}
    assert body['data'] == ''

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_response_key_count_is_exactly_eight():
    r = client.post('/post', data={'x': '1'},
                    content_type='application/x-www-form-urlencoded')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert len(body) == 8
    assert 'url' in body
    assert 'args' in body
    assert 'headers' in body
    assert 'form' in body
    assert 'data' in body
    assert 'files' in body
    assert 'json' in body
    assert 'origin' in body

tests.name: test_post_headers_reflected_in_response
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: POST to /post with a custom request header X-Custom-Test
expected: headers field in response contains the custom header key
headers field value for X-Custom-Test equals the sent value
trace: R-HTTPBIN-004: JSON body reflecting POST payload — headers field
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_headers_reflected_in_response():
    r = client.post('/post',
                    headers={'X-Custom-Test': 'sentinel-value-42'},
                    content_type='application/x-www-form-urlencoded')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    headers = body['headers']
    assert isinstance(headers, dict)
    lower_headers = {k.lower(): v for k, v in headers.items()}
    assert 'x-custom-test' in lower_headers
    assert lower_headers['x-custom-test'] == 'sentinel-value-42'

test_post_headers_reflected_in_response()
